title: Twelve Tribes Bring Equal Gifts
overview: Once the worship tent is finished, the leaders of Israel's twelve tribes bring gifts to help move it and to begin using its altar, and then God speaks to Moses there.

parts.label: Carts for moving the tent (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: With the tabernacle (the portable tent where Israel worshiped) finished, the tribal leaders gave six covered carts and twelve oxen to haul it on the journey. The earlier plans for the tent had not said how to move it, so this practical gift seems to have been the leaders' own idea, and the LORD accepted it.

parts.label: Carts shared by workload (vv. 6-9)
parts.note: The Merarites carried the heavy frames, posts and bases, so they got twice as many carts as the Gershonites, who carried the lighter curtains. The Kohathites got none, because the most holy objects, like the ark, had to be carried by hand on their shoulders.

parts.label: Twelve days for twelve tribes (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: Each tribe's leader brought his gift on his own day to dedicate the altar, that is, to mark the start of its use with the first offerings. The order follows the tribes' places around the camp, beginning with Judah on the east side.

parts.label: The same gift, twelve times (vv. 12-83)
parts.note: Each leader brings silver dishes of flour mixed with oil, a gold dish of incense, and animals for burnt offerings (burned whole), a sin offering (for cleansing from wrongdoing) and fellowship offerings (mostly eaten in a shared meal). The word-for-word repetition is likely deliberate, giving each tribe its own full record and equal honor.

parts.label: Adding it all up (vv. 84-88)
parts.note: Together the silver came to roughly 27 kilograms, the gold to over a kilogram, and the animals to 252. The text credits all of this to the twelve leaders, and some interpreters think their tribes helped pay for it, though the text does not say so.

parts.label: God speaks from the ark (v. 89)
parts.note: With the tent now in use, Moses goes in and hears God's voice from above the lid of the ark, between two golden winged figures called cherubim. The tent was meant to be the place where God meets his people, and this verse shows that purpose coming true.

think: Why might it matter to someone that their contribution is recorded in full, even when it is exactly the same as everyone else's?
